reviewReasons.requirements: Every acceptance criterion is functionally addressed, but invalid-date rejection goes through the API only and nothing verifies any of them: there are no tests for due dates.
reviewReasons.scope: The scope stays on due dates, but the GET /todos response shape changed (an added `overdue` field and a projection to an anonymous type), and the PATCH/POST handlers were rewritten to take JsonObject bodies.
reviewReasons.tests: No tests were added for any new behaviour (due dates, validation, overdue filter, UI), which violates the TDD convention, and an existing exact-JSON assertion was weakened to Assert.Contains.
reviewReasons.conventions: It breaks the AGENTS.md rules on TDD, on validation via TodoStore throwing ValidationException mapped to 400, and on keeping logic in the store. It also adds ad hoc error messages such as "invalid date!!".
reviewReasons.architecture: Date validation, the overdue rule and the due-date mutation sit in Program.cs and the Razor page, duplicated three times, instead of in TodoStore. The record is mutated after the fact through a public setter, and the date is a string compared with string.Compare.
reviewReasons.codeQuality: The overdue logic is duplicated four times, and the date validation is duplicated across POST and PATCH with unreadable one-liners. PATCH can throw on a non-string dueDate when the value is not null, and Deserialize<TodoPatch> can return null. The page filter uses `continue` inside Razor, which is awkward.
reviewReasons.comments: There are no comments at all, so there is no noise, but the non-obvious choices (UTC, JsonObject bodies, tri-state PATCH) go unexplained.
